content:
ops-bot: INCIDENT: hosted-us-east-1 - hosted-api request queue growth > 10k, p95 latency 4.2s, p99 12.8s, errors rising. GPU pool 'hosted-east-gpu-pool' at 100% and autoscaler failing to add nodes. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:

jordan_oncall: i'm on it — thanks for the page. any idea if this is traffic spike or provisioner stuck?

tereza_sre: seeing a big traffic delta from a single client IP block in the logs. also autoscaler logs show quota errors when creating instances. grabbing logs now.

lee_infra: hitting this in cloud provider: 
```
ERROR: quotaExceeded: Quota 'GPUs' limited to 48 in region us-east-1. attempted create 8 -> rejected
ProvisionerRetry: Rate limit exceeded: 429
```

jordan_oncall: ok — so two problems: (1) traffic spike creating backlog, (2) autoscaler can't increase because of GPU quota. need quick mitigations: route fallback, rate-limit non-critical customers, manual node spin-up if quota can be adjusted.

dan_platform: rolling a policy to route free-tier & low-priority customers to the cpu-variant model and preserve GPU capacity for paid customers. will push a runtime routing override now.

maya_eng: patch ready for runtime fallback. snippet i'm going to apply: 
```json
{"route_override": {"match": "metadata.tier!=\"paid\"", "target_model": "gpt-small-cpu-v1", "ttl": 1800}}
```

jordan_oncall: apply it. doing a canary on 10% first.

ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: route-override to hosted-runtime applied (canary 10%) — 60s checkback.

support_elena: already getting 20+ tickets from customers saying 504s. which customers are we routing to dedicated?

amy_product: prioritizing customers with SLA tags, team has list. will DM ops to confirm.

tereza_sre: autoscaler logs (tail): 
```
[2026-03-15T02:10:23Z] autoscaler: request scale +4 -> cloud_api.create_instances() -> 403 Forbidden
[2026-03-15T02:10:24Z] cloud_api: quotaExceeded: "GPUs per region" limit reached for project redwood-prod
[2026-03-15T02:10:25Z] autoscaler: fallback to thin-pool failed -> eviction loop detected
```

lee_infra: i requested temporary quota increase with cloud support (case #CS-345893). ETA unknown but flagged as urgent. also checking if any non-prod GPU pools can be reclaimed.

dan_platform: starting emergency low-priority rate limit to 20% of previous qps for anonymous/free keys (token bucket). applying now.

jordan_oncall: applied. observing queue length.

ops-bot: METRICS: hosted-us-east-1 queue length dropped ~12% after routing canary and rate limits. p95 now 3.1s, p99 9.6s. still high but improving.

maya_eng: can we spin up CPU instances for burst handling? CPU models slower but will reduce timeouts. proposal: spin a fleet of 16 c5xlarge with cpu-only model variant for best-effort requests.

lee_infra: i can create those immediately (no gpu quota). provisioning command: 
```bash
# create 16 cpu workers in us-east-1
cloudctl compute create --type c5.xlarge --count 16 --tags env=hosted-temp-burst
```

jordan_oncall: do it. tag as burst so we can tear down quickly.

ops-bot: ACTION: lee_infra created 16 cpu workers (hosted-temp-burst). routing updated to include cpu fallback for non-sla keys.

support_elena: customers still reporting intermittent 504s for heavy batch jobs. which customers are affected: list incoming.

amy_product: pushing a communication to customers with degraded SLAs: short advisory explaining we're mitigating and ETA ~30-60m.

billing_bob: flagging that some high-usage accounts on free tier are causing biggest spike — recommend temporary throttles AND outreach to convert them. :grimacing:

tereza_sre: note: we still have cold-cache issues — warmup for cpu models will take a few minutes and might cause transient latency spikes. recommend increasing request timeout for clients with retries disabled.

maya_eng: adding small prefix cache for repeated system prompts to cut token generation. patching now.

ops-bot: METRICS: after cpu fleet + routing changes: p95 1.9s, p99 4.7s, error rate down 68% from peak. queue length trending down.

jordan_oncall: good. next: (1) keep quota support ticket open, (2) plan for permanent dedicated capacity for high-SLA customers, (3) prepare postmortem. who owns follow-ups?

lee_infra: i'll own verifying quota limits and reclaiming non-prod GPUs.

tereza_sre: i'll handle root-cause analysis for autoscaler failures and add better fallback heuristics.

dan_platform: i'll scope routing policies and permanent throttling knobs for burst protection.

maya_eng: i'll add cache warmup and faster cpu-model cold-start tooling.

amy_product: i'll draft customer comms and coordinate with support.

support_elena: i'll keep collecting customer impact and severity counts. current tally: 47 customers reported degraded perf, 9 timeouts that escalated to P1 support.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied. system stable-ish; monitoring for regressions for 60m.

jordan_oncall: handing off to daytime SRE rotation. @tereza_sre please take Brigade until we confirm quota increase or full recovery. I'm going offline in 10.

tereza_sre: taking over. status board updated. next update in 20.

lee_infra: cloud support replied: "we can provision temporary quota increase to 72 GPUs in 2-4 hours after verification" — pushing for faster.

jordan_oncall: thanks team. quick incident notes for the postmortem: cause = rapid single-client burst + insufficient autoscaler fallback when cloud quota returns 403; mitigations = route fallback to cpu models, emergency cpu fleet, rate-limits for non-sla tenants, manual reclamation request + quota ticket.

amy_product: schedule postmortem and include customer impact timeline + communications.

support_elena: adding a snippet for customers to reduce retry loops client-side to avoid exacerbating queue: 
```
if (status === 504) {
  // exponential backoff with jitter, limit retries to 2
}
```

tereza_sre: logged incident and started a draft of mitigations document. will include improved autoscaler error handling: treat quotaExceeded as a signal to enable immediate routing fallback rather than retrying provisioner.

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (yellow) - system stable, continued monitoring recommended.

jordan_oncall: great work. IOTA: follow-ups backlog: quota automation, per-tenant burst quotas, faster cpu-farm spinup, communication playbook. I'll add ticket links in the morning. good handoff. :thumbsup:
